title: Commerce Fabric
shortDescription: CommerceFabric is a portfolio project exploring distributed systems and microservice architecture using a production-inspired eCommerce domain. The goal is not just to build an online store, but to demonstrate architectural decision-making around service boundaries, data consistency, resilience, observability, and scalability.
overview: A production-inspired microservices e-commerce platform designed to showcase service isolation, scalability, observability, and resilient event-driven integrations across distributed systems.
problem: I wanted to model a realistic e-commerce system without creating tightly coupled services, while still proving how authentication, data ownership, caching, and asynchronous events work in a modern platform.
solution: I split the platform into independent services for users, products, and orders, connected through REST APIs, message-based events, and Azure-native infrastructure. The frontend was delivered in Angular with authentication and routing handled through Azure API Management and Microsoft Entra ID.
outcome: The project demonstrates a practical architecture for fault tolerance, asynchronous communication, and scalable service boundaries in a cloud-native environment.
highlights: Built a distributed .NET microservice architecture with independent data ownership
Used Azure Service Bus and RabbitMQ to decouple domain events and improve resilience
Layered Redis caching and retry policies to reduce load and handle transient failures
Designed a production-inspired deployment model on AKS with API gateway and identity controls
